Reconstructing Visium Spatial Array Geometry

Candidate spatial-resolution models for 6.5 mm and 11 mm capture areas

Eli Spies

1 Motivation

Spatial reconstruction of spot positions in Visium non-HD Arrays

Visium spatial output provides array indices and image coordinates, but the physical placement of spot centres within the stated capture-area dimensions is not fully specified. This analysis evaluates candidate reconstructions under the reported array dimensions, spot diameter, array indexing and center-to-center distance information. Candidate geometries are tested for physical containment and non-overlap for the 6.5 mm and 11 mm Visium arrays.

Coordinate-system note. Space Ranger reports the integer indices array_row and array_col. These manufacturer-defined names are retained throughout. When visualized here, array_row is shown on the horizontal plotting axis and array_col on the vertical plotting axis. This convention can appear counter-intuitive when compared with ordinary matrix row/column terminology.

MAIL

\[ axis \in \{row, col\} \\ \text{Dimensional Constraints:} \\ L_{axis} \ \wedge \ d_{axis} \ \wedge \ d_{diag} \ \wedge \ m_{axis} \ \wedge r_{spot} \in \mathbb{R}^+ \\ n_{axis} \in \mathbb{N} \\ \text{Array Geometry:} \\ \text{C}_L: L = L_{row} = L_{col} \\ \text{C}_n: (L, n_{row}, n_{col}) \in \{(6500 \mu m, 78L, 128L), (11000 \mu m, 128L, 224L)\} \\ \text{C}_r: spot\_diameter = 55\mu m \Leftrightarrow r_{spot} = 27.5 \mu m \\ \text{C}_{diag} : d_{diag}= \sqrt{{d_{row}}^2 + {d_{col}}^2} \\ \text{C}_{noneverlap}: \left\{ \begin{matrix} d_{axis} \geq r_{spot} \\ d_{diag} = \sqrt{{d_{row}}^2 + {d_{col}}^2} \geq 2*r_{spot} \\ \end{matrix} \right.\\ \text{C}_{axis}: L_{axis}=(n_{axis}-1)*d_{axis} + 2*m_{axis} \\ \text{C}_m: m_{axis} \geq r_{spot} \models m_{axis} = r_{spot} + k_{axis}; \text{ with} \\ k_{axis} \in \mathbb{R} \ | \ 0 \leq k_{axis} \leq \frac{L_{axis}-(n_{axis}+1)*r_{spot}}{2} | \text{ C}_{nonoverlap} \wedge \text{L}_{axis} \\ \text{C}_{hex} : \text{Hexagonal grid}\\ \text{C}_{Lcr}: (\text{C}_L, \text{C}_{axis}) \models (n_{col}-1)*d_{col} + 2*k_{col} = (n_{row}-1)*d_{row} + 2*k_{row} \]

4.1.1 Fixed distance between vertical and horizontal array units

Case 1: Fixed distance of 100µm between axis units (Haxes)

\[ \text{H}_{col} \models d_{col} = 100 \mu m\\ \wedge \text{H}_{row} \models \ d_{row} = 100 \mu m \\ (\text{C}_L, \text{C}_r, \text{C}_{axis}) \models k_{axis}= \frac{L}{2}-(n_{axis}-1)*50\mu m -27.5\mu m \ (a) \\ \text{C}_{diag} \models d_{diag}=\sqrt{(100\mu m )^2 + (100\mu m )^2} = 100 \sqrt{2} \mu m \approx 141.4214 \mu m (b) \]

Case 2: Fixed distance of 100µm between vertical and horizontal spots (H2axes)

\[ \text{H}_{2col} \models d_{col} = 50 \mu m\\ \wedge \text{H}_{2row} \models \ d_{row} = 50 \mu m \\ (\text{C}_L,\text{C}_r, C_{axis}) \models k_{axis}=\frac{L}{2}-(n_{axis}-1)*25\mu m -27.5\mu m \ (a) \\ \text{C}_{diag} \models d_{diag}=\sqrt{(50\mu m )^2 + (50\mu m)^2} = 50 \sqrt{2}\mu m \approx 70.71068 \mu m (b) \]

Case 1 & 2 incompatible with Hhex: ddiag = 2dcol

\[ \text{ case 1 & case 2}:\ d_{row} = d_{col} \\ \wedge H_{diag}: d_{row} = d_{col}\sqrt{3} \\ \Leftrightarrow 1 = \sqrt{3} \quad \mathbf{\color{red}{\bot}} \implies d_{row} \neq d_{col} \]

Case 3: Distance of 100µm between diagonal with hexagonal grid (Hdiag)

$$ ({hex}, {diag}) d_{diag} = 100 m d_{col} = 50 m \ ({diag}, {hex}) d_{row} = 50 m \

(L, {axis}) L=(n_{axis}-1)d_{axis} + 2(r_{spot}+k_{axis}) \ k_{axis} = - r_{spot} \ k_{col} = - 27.5 m k_{col} = - n_{col}25m -2.5m  (a) \ k_{row} = - (n_{row}-1)(25 m)-27.5m  (b) \ $$

Hexagonal Grid

\[ \text{H}_{hex} : d_{diag}= 2d_{col} \\ \overset{\text{C}_{diag}}{\implies} \sqrt{{d_{row}}^2 + {d_{col}}^2} = 2d_{col} \\ \Leftrightarrow \ d_{row} = d_{col}\sqrt{3} \\ \]

Hexagonal Grid with ddiag = 2dcol

4.1.2 Fixed distance between selected array units & equal margins

\[ \text{Equal margins:} \\ \text{H}_{m_{equal}} : m = m_{col} = m_{row} \implies k = k_{col} = k_{row} \\ \]

Case 4: Distance of 50µm between vertical array units

\[ \text{H}_{2col} \models d_{col} = 50 \mu m \\ \text{H}_{m_{equal}} \models m = m_{row} = m_{col} \implies k = k_{col} = k_{row} \\ (\text{C}_L, \text{C}_r, \text{C}_{col},\text{H}_{2col},\text{H}_{m_{equal}}) \models k =\frac{L}{2}-(n_{col}-1)*25 \mu m -27.5\mu m \ (a) \\ (\text{C}_{Lcr}, \text{H}_{2col}, \text{H}_{m_{equal}}) \models (n_{col}-1)*50 \mu m = (n_{row}-1)*d_{row} \\ \Leftrightarrow \ d_{row}= \frac{n_{col}-1}{n_{row}-1}*50 \mu m \ (b) \ \\ \text{C}_{diag} \models d_{diag} = \sqrt{(50 \mu m)^2 + (\frac{n_{col}-1}{n_{row}-1}*50 \mu m)^2} \\ \Leftrightarrow d_{diag} = 50 \mu m * \sqrt{1+(\frac{n_{col}-1}{n_{row}-1})^2} \ (c) \]

4.2 Margin-derived models

Fixed-margin equations

\[ \text{H}_{100} \text{ optional:} \\ (\text{C}_L, \text{C}_{axis}, \text{C}_{m}) \models \ L=d_{axis}*(n_{axis}-1) + 2*(r_{spot} + k_{axis}) \\ \Leftrightarrow \ d_{axis} = \frac{L - 2*(r_{spot} + k_{axis})}{n_{axis}-1} (I) \\ (\text{C}_{diag}, \text{C}_{m}) \models \ d_{diag}= \sqrt{(\frac{L - 2*r_{spot} - 2*k_{col}}{n_{col}-1})^2 + (\frac{L - 2*r_{spot} -2*k_{row}}{n_{row}-1})^2} \ (II) \]

Case 5: Minimal margins (kmin)

\[ \text{H}{_{k_{min}}}: k=0 \mu m \\ (I) \ d_{axis} = \frac{L - 2r_{spot}}{n_{axis}-1} (a) \\ (II) \ d_{diag}= \sqrt{(\frac{L - 2r_{spot}}{n_{col}-1})^2 + (\frac{L - 2r_{spot}}{n_{row}-1})^2} \\ \Leftrightarrow \ d_{diag}= \sqrt{(\frac{L - 2r_{spot}}{n_{col}-1})^2 + (\frac{L - 2r_{spot}}{n_{row}-1})^2} \\ \Leftrightarrow \ d_{diag}= \frac{L- 2r_{spot}}{(n_{col}-1)*(n_{row}-1)}*\sqrt{(n_{col}-1)^2 + (n_{row}-1)^2} \ (b) \] —

4.2.1 Axis-distance-margin relation

Case 6: 1:1-relation (daxis = maxis)

\[ \text{H}_{d:m}: d_{axis}=m_{axis} \\ \text{H}_{d:m} \models\ m_{col} = d_{col} \wedge\ m_{row} = d_{row} \\ \implies k_{col} =d_{col}-r_{spot} \wedge k_{row}=d_{row}-r_{spot} \\ (\text{C}_L, \text{C}_{col}, \text{H}_{d:m}) \models \ L=d_{col}*(n_{col}-1) + 2d_{col} \\ \Leftrightarrow \ d_{col} = \frac{L}{n_{col}+1} (a) \\ (\text{C}_L, \text{C}_{row}, \text{H}_{d:m}) \models \ L=d_{row}*(n_{row}-1) + 2d_{row} \\ \Leftrightarrow \ d_{row} = \frac{L}{n_{row}+1} (b) \\ (\text{C}_{diag}, \text{H}_{d:m}) \models \ d_{diag}= \sqrt{(\frac{L}{n_{col}+1})^2 + (\frac{L}{n_{row}+1})^2} \\ \Leftrightarrow \ d_{diag}= \frac{L*\sqrt{(n_{col}+1)^2 + (n_{row}+1)^2}}{(n_{col}+1)*(n_{row}+1)} (c) \]

5 Visium Array results

Utilizing the previous equations for calculating the array-specific values, we can check, whether each case would be geometrically feasible (case_possible) under the assumption that the nominal values of each capture area, namely 6.5mm for the small and 11mm for the large non-HD Visium Array, must include all complete 55-µm spots.

5.1 Small non-HD Array (6.5mm)

\[ \text{C}_{L}: L = L_{row} = L_{col} = 6500\mu m \\ \text{C}_{n}: (L, n_{row}, n_{col}) \in \{(6500 \mu m, 78L, 128L) \\ \text{C}_{r}: spot\_diameter = 55\mu m \Leftrightarrow r_{spot} = 27.5 \mu m \\ \text{C}_{m}: m_{axis} \geq r_{spot} \models m_{axis} = r_{spot} + k_{axis}; \text{ with} \\ k_{axis} \in \mathbb{R} \ | \ 0 \leq k_{axis} \leq \frac{L_{axis}-(n_{axis}+1)*r_{spot}}{2} | \text{ C}_{nonoverlap} \wedge \text{L}_{axis} \\ \implies k_{max_{col}} = \frac{6500 \mu m-129*27.5\mu m}{2} = 1476.25 \mu m \\ \wedge k_{max_{row}} = \frac{6500 \mu m-79*27.5\mu m}{2} = 2163.75 \mu m \]

\[ \text{C}_{L}: L = L_{row} = L_{col} = 11000\mu m \\ \text{C}_{n}: (L, n_{row}, n_{col}) \in \{(11000 \mu m, 128L, 224L) \\ \text{C}_{r}: spot\_diameter = 55\mu m \Leftrightarrow r_{spot} = 27.5 \mu m \\ \text{C}_{m}: m_{axis} \geq r_{spot} \models m_{axis} = r_{spot} + k_{axis}; \text{ with} \\ k_{axis} \in \mathbb{R} \ | \ 0 \leq k_{axis} \leq \frac{L_{axis}-(n_{axis}+1)*r_{spot}}{2} | \text{ C}_{nonoverlap} \wedge \text{L}_{axis} \\ \implies k_{max_{col}} = \frac{11000 \mu m-225*27.5\mu m}{2} = 2406.25 \mu m \\ \wedge k_{max_{row}} = \frac{11000 \mu m-129*27.5\mu m}{2} = 3726.25 \mu m \]
